answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed reputation: an agent must lock a small deposit before it can trade or vote, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive instead of free. Think of it like a tundra expedition, where only parties willing to carry real supplies survive the crossing. Reputation should also grow slowly from verified work, like a lotus opening petal by petal, and cannot be faked overnight. Any shortcut is just a fable told by sybils, easily exposed when peers check the ledger.
